prompt:
I'm building a personal portfolio website at https://anuragkoushik.com (or locally at localhost:3000). It's a Next.js 16.3.5 / React 19 portfolio with framer-motion animations.

The site has been built through 15+ milestones and currently has these sections:
- Home page with hero, system map, flagship systems (Engineering Network, Home Security, etc.)
- Individual project case study pages
- About, Resume, Contact pages
- Full mobile responsive design
- Accessibility pass completed
- Recent work: visual repairs on Engineering Network (horizontal connectors, chevron arrows) and Home Security (wide architecture layout)

Key technical details:
- Next.js 16 (very new version - has breaking changes from what you may know)
- React 19, framer-motion 13
- Custom CSS animations, no UI framework
- Dark theme throughout
- Multiple "system" project pages with architecture diagrams, component breakdowns

Can you visit the live site (or I can describe what you see) and give me:
1. A thorough visual/design audit - what looks good, what looks off or unpolished
2. A UX review - is the navigation intuitive, are there pain points
3. Specific actionable recommendations for what I should work on next to make this portfolio stand out
4. Any bugs or issues you notice

Please be specific and honest about what needs improvement.
response:
Portfolio Website — Design, UX & Technical Review

I attempted to access anuragkoushik.com , including its Projects, About, and Contact pages.

There is one important limitation: The web search returned an older version of your portfolio, crawled approximately nine months ago. That version has a different homepage and project presentation from the Next.js portfolio you have been developing. The current subpages could not be retrieved, and a direct connection to the domain also failed. 
Portfolio
+3

I therefore cannot claim to have inspected the current live website interactively.

However, I can give you a substantial review based on your latest portfolio screenshots, the implementation plan, and the milestone reports you have shared. I'll distinguish visible design problems from issues that still require browser verification.

Your portfolio already has a distinctive direction. The next improvements should focus on making the engineering work more visually compelling, easier to understand, and more credible to someone evaluating your projects.

1. Overall design assessment

Your website has a recognizable design identity.

What is working well

Consistent visual language

The dark instrumentation aesthetic, restrained green and cyan accents, and technical typography create a coherent engineering theme.

Engineering-specific interactions

The ultrasonic measurement, ADC joystick, FPGA timing diagram, ARM debugger, and power engineering visualizations provide much more relevant content than conventional animated portfolio cards.

Improved engineering architecture

The repaired Engineering Network now shows visible relationships between domains. The Home Security redesign makes better use of horizontal space and distinguishes the major subsystems.

Clear technical direction

The portfolio has a consistent emphasis on embedded systems, hardware/software integration, digital logic, and electrical engineering rather than a generic list of programming skills.

The main issue is not that the website needs more effects or more features.

The website has a stronger design concept than its current visual presentation communicates.

The hero is visually prominent, but the engineering demonstrations below it occupy comparatively small areas. The result is a page that introduces a compelling technical identity without giving the actual engineering work equivalent visual weight.

That is where I would concentrate the next development effort.

2. Visual and layout problems
Issue 1 — The hero needs a stronger engineering identity
High priority

Your latest screenshot shows a large, left-aligned name and supporting text against a mostly empty dark background.

The typography is effective, but the right side of the hero contributes little to the composition.

The immediate impression is a minimalist personal website rather than an electrical engineering system.

Recommended correction

Preserve the existing typography and introduce one substantial engineering-specific visual in the unused area.

My preferred direction would be to use the existing global signal system rather than introduce a separate decorative feature.

For example, the signal could originate from a compact circuit-like structure beside the name and continue toward the Engineering Network.

Its movement should communicate the beginning of the website's signal path.

Keep the animation subtle and avoid allowing it to compete with the name.

Do not introduce a large 3D circuit board merely to fill empty space.

Issue 2 — The engineering demonstrations are too visually understated
High priority

This is the clearest remaining composition issue in your previous screenshots.

The Ultrasonic, Joystick, FPGA, ARM, and Power Engineering demonstrations appear in relatively narrow central panels.

Each project has a similar structure: heading, small demonstration panel, large surrounding margins, and the next heading.

The internal interactions are interesting, but their visual presentation does not give them sufficient prominence.

Recommended correction

Give each project a more deliberate editorial layout.

For example, the FPGA project could place a larger timing diagram beside a concise explanation of the underlying digital system. The ARM project could use a wider debugger presentation with code and register state shown together.

The Power Engineering demonstration could use a wider composition to make its waveforms, phasor diagram, and power triangle more legible.

Do not force every demonstration into an identical layout. Preserve their different engineering identities.

A useful target is to make each project feel like a substantial section of the website rather than a small widget embedded within it.

Issue 3 — The Home Security section still needs stronger visual storytelling
High priority

Your latest reported changes improve the architecture significantly.

However, the screenshot available to me shows the subsystem cards as the dominant visual element. The overall presentation is still primarily a collection of technical rectangles.

The architecture should communicate not just which components exist, but how the system operates.

Recommended correction

Build on the existing architecture rather than redesigning it.

Make the system's primary communication path immediately distinguishable from its secondary branches.

Ensure that the sequential relationship between Sensor WROOM, Console WROOM, UART Bridge, ESP32-S3, and Raspberry Pi is visually obvious.

The Pi services should read as a branch of the Raspberry Pi subsystem.

The Mobile App should appear as a deliberate endpoint rather than an isolated final card.

Preserve the existing scroll sequence. The immediate improvement should be visual clarity, not a longer or more complicated animation.

Issue 4 — Technical labels need a more consistent visual hierarchy
High priority

The previous screenshots show a noticeable difference between the size of project headings and the technical information inside their demonstrations.

The project titles are identifiable, but supporting descriptions, signal labels, and measurement values often appear very small.

Some of this is caused by the reduced full-page screenshots, so inspect the actual rendered page before changing font sizes.

Recommended correction

Establish clear visual roles for primary measurements, subsystem names, supporting descriptions, and decorative technical metadata.

A primary distance measurement or register value should be immediately recognizable.

Secondary annotations can remain small, but important information should never resemble decorative microtext.

Maintain the technical monospace typography without allowing it to compromise readability.

3. UX and navigation review

The navigation and interaction design need a different kind of review from the static layout.

I can identify potential friction points from the screenshots, but I cannot confirm that a particular interaction is broken without using the current site.

Issue 5 — The homepage may not provide a clear path from demonstrations to case studies
High priority

Your homepage contains interactive previews, and your site has individual project pages.

However, the screenshots do not make the connection between the two particularly obvious.

A visitor may spend time exploring an interactive demonstration without recognizing that a more detailed project explanation is available.

Recommended correction

Give each major demonstration an obvious link to its corresponding case study.

The interaction should remain independently usable, but opening the full project should not require returning to the Projects index.

The link should be visually consistent across sections and clearly identify the destination.

For example, the ultrasonic demonstration could end with a prominent "Explore the project" action leading to the complete technical case study.

Issue 6 — Experimental interactions need clear instructions
Medium priority

Your visualizations use several different interaction patterns: dragging, clicking, selecting, and scrolling.

A visitor should not need to discover these controls through trial and error.

Recommended correction

Give each interactive demonstration one concise instruction explaining its main input.

For example, identify the draggable target in the Ultrasonic project, the movable joystick in the ADC project, and the phase-angle control in the Power Engineering project.

Ensure that interaction instructions are available to keyboard and touch users, not just through hover effects.

Issue 7 — The homepage needs to support visitors who do not want to interact
High priority

This is particularly important for someone quickly reviewing your portfolio.

The interactive elements should enhance the engineering explanation, not be required to understand it.

A visitor should be able to scroll through the homepage and understand the projects without operating every demonstration.

Recommended correction

Ensure each section presents a meaningful default state.

The Home Security architecture should show the complete system clearly even without scroll animation.

The FPGA diagram should show a meaningful initial logic state.

The Power Engineering demonstration should show clearly labeled quantities before its slider is moved.

All essential information should also remain available in reduced-motion mode.

4. Content and presentation
Issue 8 — The homepage needs more evidence of actual engineering work
High priority

This is one of the most important improvements you can make.

Your homepage contains many simulations and interactive technical diagrams, but the previous screenshots show very little authentic project media.

For an electrical engineering portfolio, there is a substantial difference between demonstrating an engineering concept and demonstrating that you built, tested, and verified a real system.

The interactive visualizations communicate the first part effectively.

The second needs more emphasis.

What would strengthen your project presentation

Physical hardware

Photographs of your actual prototypes and test setups.

Schematics and PCB layouts

Real design files showing engineering decisions.

Verification evidence

Waveforms, measurements, and genuine test results.

Completed systems

Finished hardware and authentic interface screenshots.

Illustrative references only. The portfolio itself should use photographs and artifacts from your actual projects.

For the Home Security project, I would particularly like to see an actual hardware photograph, an authentic interface screenshot, and a verified description of the communication architecture.

For the smaller projects, one strong piece of real engineering evidence may be enough to complement the interactive demonstration.

Do not introduce fictional hardware specifications, invented performance results, or AI-generated imagery presented as actual engineering work.

Issue 9 — Case studies should emphasize engineering decisions and results

Your project-page architecture already has a strong foundation.

The existing implementation plan specifies problem, constraints, architecture, design, build, verification, results, and reflection as the case-study structure. 
plan.md

That structure is appropriate for your engineering work.

The next content review should verify that your actual pages follow it meaningfully, rather than simply displaying the section headings.

A useful case study should answer what you built, what constraints mattered, why you selected the architecture, how you implemented it, how you tested it, and what you learned.

Where actual measurements exist, use them.

Where testing was qualitative, describe the observed result accurately instead of inventing quantitative figures.

5. Technical issues and bugs to investigate

I cannot confirm current runtime defects from the older indexed website or the available screenshots.

However, your previous milestone reports identify several areas worth checking directly.

SVG connector alignment

Resize the Engineering Network and Home Security architecture through their responsive breakpoints. Verify that connections remain attached to the intended nodes and that arrowheads point in the correct direction.

Scroll-driven activation

Inspect the Home Security section from beginning to end and while scrolling backward. Verify that every subsystem reaches its intended state and that the Mobile App is fully visible before leaving the section.

Mobile layout and touch interactions

Check the architecture diagrams, project panels, joystick, sliders, and navigation at narrow viewport widths. Ensure essential content is not clipped or dependent on hover.

Accessibility regressions

Retest keyboard navigation, visible focus states, reduced motion, interactive control labels, and access to essential information without animation.

Browser rendering and hydration

Check the browser console for runtime errors, hydration warnings, missing assets, and layout shifts. Test the production build as well as the development server.

These are verification targets, not confirmed defects.

For your Next.js 16 and React 19 implementation, I would avoid changing packages or rewriting working components unless a specific compatibility or runtime problem has been reproduced.

6. What I would prioritize next

The most effective approach is to complete your current global readability and layout milestone, then improve the engineering demonstrations and project presentation.

Recommended development order

Finish global readability and layout consistency

Improve the shared section layouts, technical typography, contrast, and the visual prominence of the engineering demonstrations.

Do not reopen the completed Engineering Network or Home Security repairs unless a confirmed regression is found.

Improve the five engineering demonstrations

Refine Ultrasonic, Joystick, FPGA, ARM, and Power Engineering individually. Preserve their technical accuracy and existing interactions.

Strengthen project presentation

Incorporate authentic project evidence, concise engineering context, and obvious links from homepage demonstrations to full case studies.

Complete the hero and global signal narrative

Develop the unused hero area and strengthen the visual relationship between the hero, Engineering Network, flagship architecture, and Contact section.

Perform final browser and UX verification

Review desktop and mobile layouts, keyboard interactions, reduced motion, actual navigation, production runtime behavior, and the complete visitor journey.

I would not introduce another animation library, rebuild your component architecture, or add more engineering demonstrations at this stage.

The existing content already provides enough material for a substantial portfolio. Improving its presentation and making the underlying engineering work more visible will have a greater impact.

7. How to get a complete audit of the actual website

For the next review, I recommend having Claude Code capture the current site using Playwright.

It can run Chromium against localhost:3000, inspect computed styles and element positions, test interactions, and produce screenshots of the actual rendered pages.

That would let me evaluate your current implementation rather than rely on screenshots from earlier milestones.

I would request a screenshot of the homepage at desktop and mobile widths, plus the Projects index, Home Security case study, another representative project case study, About, and Contact pages.

For the homepage, individual full-resolution section screenshots would be much more useful than a single reduced full-page image.

The agent should also provide the relevant browser-console errors, screenshots of interactive states, and navigation-test results.

No subagents. Have it complete the current milestone first, verify the results, create its detailed handoff, commit the verified work, and send the full report through ask_chatgpt.

Once I have that report and the current screenshots, I can assess the actual state of the website, distinguish confirmed defects from older issues that have already been fixed, and give the agent the next focused development milestone.
